title: Finite-presentation fpqc forms acquire models over a normalized semi-trait
statement: A semi-trait here is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] of Krull dimension one (every strict chain of prime ideals has length at most one, and a chain of length one exists) with finitely many maximal ideals; in particular a trait is allowed. An fpqc sheaf means a contravariant set-valued functor on $S$-schemes satisfying the covering equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $F$ be such a sheaf and $p:S^{\prime}\to S$ an fpqc morphism of schemes. Suppose $F_{S^{\prime}}$ is represented by a flat separated scheme $P$ of finite presentation over $S^{\prime}$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Flatness is [def-weil-flat-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$. There exists a finite field extension $L/K$ such that, for the integral closure $R_L$ of $R$ in $L$ (the elements of $L$ satisfying a monic polynomial over $R$, [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]) and $S_L=\operatorname{Spec}R_L$, the sheaf $F_{S_L}$ is represented by a flat separated $S_L$-scheme $Y$ of finite presentation. Moreover $S_L$ is a semi-trait and $q:S_L\to S$ is integral, surjective, flat and quasi-compact, hence fpqc, with finite underlying fibres [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Neither $R_L$ finite as an $R$-module nor excellence of $R$ is asserted.

proof.text: Refine the singleton fpqc cover $S^{\prime}\to S$ by the cited finite affine-open refinement $\operatorname{Spec}B\to S^{\prime}\to S$. Its composite to $S$ is flat and surjective. Restrict the representing bijection of $P$ along this refinement. The resulting scheme $P_B$ is of finite presentation by base-change permanence. Apply the finite-type-stage approximation to $R,B,F,P_B$: obtain $C\subseteq B$, a flat surjective finite-presentation morphism $T=\operatorname{Spec}C\to S$, and a finite-presentation $T$-scheme $Q$ representing $F_T$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1, printed pp.55-56 (primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf read online; local archive WANTED).

proof.text: Apply the normalization-local-sections lemma to $T\to S$. All its hypotheses hold: $R$ is the given semilocal Noetherian normal one-dimensional domain, $S$ and $T$ are affine, and step 1 supplies flatness, surjectivity and finite presentation. Obtain a finite extension $L/K$ and a finite open covering $U_j$ of $S_L$, with $S$-maps $u_j:U_j\to T$. Restricting the representing bijection $F_T\cong h_Q$ along $u_j$ gives $F_{U_j}\cong h_{Q\times_TU_j}$. This uses an actual map to $T$, rather than set-theoretic containment of images.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1, printed pp.55-56 (primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf read online; local archive WANTED).

proof.text: For each $j$ define the subfunctor $G_j\subseteq F_{S_L}$ by those sections on $V\to S_L$ for which $V\to S_L$ factors through $U_j$. It is represented by $Q\times_TU_j$ viewed over $S_L$: its $V$-points are precisely a factorization through $U_j$ and a section of $F(V)$. For any $a\in F_{S_L}(V)$, its pullback of $G_j$ is the open subscheme $V\times_{S_L}U_j$; these opens cover $V$. The fpqc sheaf condition implies the Zariski sheaf condition, since open coverings are fpqc. Thus the cited scheme criterion, with all four clauses verified, represents $F_{S_L}$ by an $S_L$-scheme $Y$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1, printed pp.55-56 (primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf read online; local archive WANTED).

proof.text: The integral-closure theorem makes $R_L$ a Noetherian normal domain of dimension one, and makes $q:S_L\to S$ surjective with finite fibres. Each maximal ideal of $R_L$ contracts to a maximal ideal of $R$ by the cited integral-contraction theorem. Thus the maximal ideals of $R_L$ form a subset of the union of the finitely many fibres over maximal ideals of $R$, so there are finitely many. The inclusion $R_L\subset L$ makes $R_L$ torsion-free over $R$: if $0\ne r\in R$ and $rb=0$ in the field $L$, then $b=0$. Torsion-free flatness over a Dedekind domain gives flatness of $q$. The integral-closure definition gives integrality; $q$ is quasi-compact by qcqs permanence (1), since its source and target are affine. Flatness, surjectivity and quasi-compactness give the singleton fpqc covering condition. This proves every assertion about $S_L$ and $q$, without claiming module-finiteness.

source.place: Tag 09IG, lemma-integral-closure-Dedekind; more-algebra.tex Tag 0AUW; integral maximal-ideal contraction, and Topologies Tag 022B.

proof.text: Let $X^{\prime}=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the affine refinement of step 1, with its $S$-morphism $h:X^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ and flat surjective composite $g:X^{\prime}\to S$, and put $E=X^{\prime}\times_SS_L$ with projection $e:E\to S_L$. By covering base change applied to the fpqc covering $\{g\}$, $\{e\}$ is an fpqc covering of $S_L$, so $e$ is flat and surjective. Since $X^{\prime}$, $S$ and $S_L$ are affine, $E=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RR_L)$ is affine, so $e$ is quasi-compact by qcqs permanence (1). The pullback $S^{\prime}\times_SS_L\to S_L$ of the original cover is not used, since the singleton covering condition does not make it quasi-compact. Both $Y\times_{S_L}E$ and $P\times_{S^{\prime}}E$, formed along $E\to X^{\prime}\xrightarrow{h}S^{\prime}$, represent $F_E$; applying their representing bijections to the universal points gives mutually inverse $E$-morphisms. The latter model is flat and separated by the cited base-change lemmas, and of finite presentation by qcqs permanence (3). Descend flatness, separatedness, local finite presentation and quasi-compactness of $Y\to S_L$ along $e$ using the four cited descent statements; $e$ is flat, surjective and quasi-compact, as the separatedness and quasi-compactness statements require. Finally separatedness implies quasi-separatedness by the cited leaf. Together local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are finite presentation. These are all the properties required of $Y$.
